blocks.content: Now, let's combine everything we've done so far into a full-fledged executable program.

1# a class to create and add nodes
2class TreeNode:
3    def __init__(self, data):
4        self.data = data
5        self.children = []
6
7    def add_child(self, child):
8        self.children.append(child)
9
10# a class to create tree and perform tree operations
11class Tree:
12    def __init__(self, root=None):
13        self.root = root
14
15# create the root node
16root = TreeNode("Book")
17
18# create children of root
19child1 = TreeNode(1)
20child2 = TreeNode(2)
21child3 = TreeNode(3)
22
23# create leaf nodes
24child1_1 = TreeNode(1.1)
25child1_2 = TreeNode(1.2)
26child1_3 = TreeNode(1.3)
27child1_4 = TreeNode(1.4)
28child2_1 = TreeNode(2.1)
29child3_1 = TreeNode(3.1)
30child3_2 = TreeNode(3.2)
31child3_3 = TreeNode(3.3)
32
33# describe relationships between the nodes
34# and add children to the root node
35root.add_child(child1)
36root.add_child(child2)
37root.add_child(child3)
38
39# add children to child1
40child1.add_child(child1_1)
41child1.add_child(child1_2)
42child1.add_child(child1_3)
43child1.add_child(child1_4)
44
45# add children to child2
46child2.add_child(child2_1)
47
48# add children to child3
49child3.add_child(child3_1)
50child3.add_child(child3_2)
51child3.add_child(child3_3)
52
53# create the tree
54general_tree = Tree(root)
If you run this program, the output will be empty.
We will learn to traverse a tree to get individual nodes in the next lesson. For now, let's add print statements to get an idea of how this code works.
